away.name: Mackenzie Blackwood
away.news: Scott Wedgewood recorded a shutout in his most recent game, arguably his first strong performance of the season, but in consecutive games since, Colorado will return to Blackwood, who has been their go-to guy all season. The 29-year-old Blackwood is coming off a 28-save outing for his second shutout of the season, a dominant 6-0 win over the Montreal Canadiens. The Avalanche enter Friday's game as slight +102 road underdogs against the Minnesota Wild.

home.name: Jesper Wallstedt
home.news: Filip Gustavsson returned earlier this week, but the team seems comfortable continuing to lean on Wallstedt, who has deservedly been the NHL's busiest goalie this season. That said, Wallstedt is coming off one of his weakest performances of the season, allowing four goals on 21 shots (.810 SV%) in a 4-3 loss to the Utah Mammoth. Minnesota enters Friday's game as slight -112 home favourites against the Colorado Avalanche.

away.name: Darcy Kuemper
away.news: Kuemper has been far from stellar this season, but through 22 games, he remains the only goalie with a win for the Kings. That said, the 36-year-old veteran goalie saved 29 of 30 shots (.967 SV%) in his most recent game, a 2-1 win over the Montreal Canadiens. He has won three straight games while saving 82 of 86 shots (.953 SV%). The Kings enter Friday's game as slight -113 road favourites against the Anaheim Ducks.

home.name: Laurent Brossoit
home.news: Brossoit had a successful stint with the Ducks earlier this month, but was surprisingly sent down to San Diego (AHL) after a 4-2 loss to the Nashville Predators on November 11th, when he allowed four goals on 22 shots (.818 SV%). In his return to action on Wednesday, Brossoit made a strong case for staying in the NHL, recording the Ducks' first shutout of the season with 23 saves in a 7-0 win over the San Jose Sharks. The Ducks enter Friday's game as slight -104 home underdogs against the Los Angeles Kings, who are coming off a 2-1 win over the Montreal Canadiens.

away.name: Carter Hart
away.news: Hart has won four of his last five (4-1-0) but has been far from stellar, allowing three or more goals in four of those games. The 28-year-old goalie allowed four goals on 24 shots (.875 SV%) in his most recent game, a 5-3 win over the Edmonton Oilers. The Golden Knights enter Friday’s game as sizeable -206 road favourites against the San Jose Sharks.

home.name: Yaroslav Askarov
home.news: Askarov was serviceable in his most recent game, saving 26 of 29 shots (.897 SV%), but his team fell to a 5-2 loss to the Minnesota Wild. The 24-year-old Russian goalie has been far from spectacular this season, but has given his team a chance more often than not. In his last 14 games, Askarov has played much better than his 4-7-1 record suggests, posting a 2.97 GAA and .903 SV%. The Sharks enter Friday's game as +179 home underdogs against the Vegas Golden Knights.

away.name: Dylan Garand
away.news: Despite losing 5-2 to the Carolina Hurricanes in his most recent outing, Garand was solid, saving 36 of 40 shots (.900 SV%). The 24-year-old rookie goalie has allowed three or fewer goals in six of his last seven games (3-4-0), posting a solid .919 SV%. The Rangers enter Friday's game as -178 road favourites against the Chicago Blackhawks.

home.name: Spencer Knight
home.news: After a solid inaugural full season with Chicago in 2025-26, posting a 2.82 GAA and .902 SV% in 55 games (19-25-11), Knight has struggled in 2026-27. That said, he's in his best stretch of the season, winning three of his last four (3-1-0), posting a 2.47 GAA and .924 SV%. The Blackhawks enter Friday's game as +153 home underdogs against the New York Rangers.

home.name: Semyon Varlamov
home.news: After missing the entire 2025-26 season due to an injury, Varlamov's return to the crease in 2026-27 has been inconsistent. The veteran 38-year-old goalie struggled in his most recent outing, allowing four goals on 22 shots (.818 SV%) in a 4-3 overtime loss to the Winnipeg Jets. That said, he has helped his team record a point in six of his last seven games (2-1-3). The Islanders enter Friday's game as -117 home favourites in a rematch against the Jets, who are 9-1-1 in their past 11 games.

away.name: Sergei Murashov
away.news: The Penguins are having a miserable season, but the lightly used Murashov has shown some encouraging signs between the pipes. The 22-year-old rookie goalie had a poor outing, allowing four goals on 29 shots (.862 SV%) in a 4-3 loss to the Nashville Predators. The loss ended a solid three-game stretch for Murashov (2-1-0), in which he saved 91 of 98 shots (.929 SV%). The Penguins enter Friday's game as +126 road underdogs against the Buffalo Sabres.

away.name: Philipp Grubauer
away.news: Grubauer has had ups and downs in the 2026-27 season and is coming off a poor performance, allowing four goals on 28 shots (.857 SV%) in a 4-3 loss to the San Jose Sharks. Still, the 35-year-old German goalie has a decent 2.59 GAA and .908 SV% in five November appearances (1-3-0). The Kraken enter Friday's game as +182 road underdogs against the Edmonton Oilers.

home.name: Tristan Jarry
home.news: After a disappointing introduction to the Oilers in the 2025-26 season, Jarry has been reliable on most nights in 2026-27. That said, he struggled in his most recent game, allowing four goals on 27 shots (.852 SV%) in a 5-4 shootout loss to the St. Louis Blues. It snapped a six-game stretch in which Jarry allowed three or fewer goals in each game (4-0-2). The Oilers enter Friday's outing as -203 home favourites against the Seattle Kraken, who are coming off a 3-1 loss to the Chicago Blackhawks.
